title: Adaptive Audit Schema Layer & Change-Signal Mitigation Playbook
body:
Purpose
This doc proposes an Adaptive Schema Layer (ASL) that sits between Redwood producers (runtime, console, ded-controllers) and consumers (SIEM, evidence-store, analytics pipelines). The ASL goal is to: 1) reduce noisy change signals when fields evolve, 2) provide lightweight compatibility guarantees, and 3) make evidence automation into SIEM exports resilient to rolling changes (RBAC v2 field enrichment, new evidence handles, payload minification).

Context / motivation
- We continue to see frequent schema churn as new audit attributes (role_context, session_affinity, model_variant) are added by product/infra teams. Consumers (security analytics, compliance exports) are brittle and generate high-volume incidents when a minor field name/type shifts.
- Existing pattern: producer publishes an event, consumers implement mapping fixes on demand (ad-hoc). This results in: missed evidence, SIEM alerts, and emergency rollbacks.
- ASL should be designed for quick producer iteration while providing clear, semantic guarantees to downstream consumers.

High-level design
1) Canonical core event envelope (Core v1): a small, strongly-typed subset every producer must include. Fields: timestamp_utc, event_id (UUIDv7 if available), actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (success/failure/partial). Core must be stable and backwards-compatible across minor revisions.
2) Adaptive layer (Adapt v1): free-form extension area (map of string->any) plus structured adapters. This is where producers can attach new attributes without breaking core contract. Each attribute MUST include provenance metadata: source_component, schema_tag, schema_version.
3) Contract signals: semantic change-signal headers emitted with publish time. Example header: X-Audit-Signal: change=added:resource_label;tag=infra:v2. Consumers can decide to ignore or trigger migrations based on policy.
4) Consumer adapters: each consuming subsystem registers an adapter that performs 3 things: a) soft-parse adapt fields using schema_tag heuristics, b) validate core fields, c) surface a normalized artifact to downstream pipelines.

Why this differs from current approach
- We do not force a monolithic schema registry or synchronous gating for every field addition. Instead we add metadata + signaling so consumers can opt-in to enforcement.
- The adapt area intentionally supports both typed and untyped payloads, enabling rapid product iteration while preserving an auditable provenance chain.

Integration with RBAC v2
- RBAC v2 introduces richer context (role_changes, policy_snapshot, delegated_principal). These should live in the adapt layer with a required schema_tag: rbac_v2/{minor}.{patch}. Producers must include a policy_snapshot_ref that points to a snapshot id stored in evidence-store (or inline if small).
- For critical RBAC events (permission_grant, permission_revoke), enforce core-level outcome semantics and include a stable action taxonomy: rbac.grant | rbac.revoke | rbac.assert. Consumer adapters for SIEM should expand policy_snapshot_ref into normalized fields used by detection rules (e.g., delta_count, approver_id).

Evidence automation & SIEM export implications
- Export profiles: each customer/SIEM mapping will use a named profile (e.g., external-splunk-v1, datadog-security-v2). Profiles declare which schema_tags they care about and transformation rules.
- Buffering and backpressure: ASL will emit an export manifest per-batch that includes schema_tags present. SIEM exporters can apply backpressure or route to a staging pipeline when unknown tags are dominant.
- Redaction/minification: ASL can apply configurable redaction policies per-profile to ensure PII/privacy compliance prior to export. Keep original raw artifact in evidence-store (immutable) and push a redacted copy to SIEM.

Versioning and change-signal lifecycle
- Semantic vs syntactic changes: classify each change signal as syntactic (field rename/type change) or semantic (meaning change). Syntactic changes should carry a compat_hint (rename/from:old_field). Semantic changes require an opt-in migration period with at least 2 weeks of dual-write where producers write both old and new attributes.
- Signal levels: info | advisory | breaking. Producers include level in X-Audit-Signal. Consumer adapters expose a migration API that can subscribe to advisory signals.
- Deprecation schedule: when marking a field deprecated, producers must: a) emit advisory signal for >=14 days, b) emit warning header for >=7 days, c) remove only after a coordinated rollout and consumer opt-in recorded. All events must be logged to change-tracker (ticket id).

Operational tooling and telemetry
- ASL health metrics: unknown_schema_tag_rate, adapt_field_error_rate, consumer-parser-latency, dual-write-coverage.
- Signal dashboard: a simple UI in Console for listing active schema_tags, their producers, subscribers, and deprecation status.
- Contract tests: producers will run a lightweight contract test suite that verifies Core invariants and at least a basic parse of registered adapt schema_tags. CI to block major releases until tests pass for impacted profiles.

Migration playbook (producer-facing)
1) Design new attribute and pick schema_tag (team/component/name:v{major}.{minor}).
2) Add attribute in adapt area; include provenance metadata and compat_hint if renaming.
3) Emit X-Audit-Signal: change=added:team_label;tag=team_label:v1;level=advisory.
4) Run unit contract tests that parse the adapt payload.
5) Announce via #sec-schema-change and file JIRA migration ticket listing consumer profiles.
6) Dual-write: write both old and new attribute for minimum 14 days (longer for critical events).
7) After consumer confirmation, mark deprecation and schedule removal.

Consumer guidance (SIEM / evidence-store / compliance)
- Always parse Core fields first and route on stable keys.
- Treat adapt as optional; do not fail ingestion on unknown tags. Instead, surface them to the unknown_tag queue for triage.
- Implement adapters that can be updated independently from ingestion code. Adapter updates are low-risk and can be rolled without changing producers.

Open questions / unresolved items
- Do we mandate UUIDv7 for event_id or accept whatever producers send? (Pros/cons to be documented).
- How to ensure evidence-store snapshot ids are efficiently retrievable by SIEM exporters without increasing tail-latency? Possible solution: small inline snapshots for <2KB.
- What is the enforcement model for producers that ignore advisory signals? Should we auto-suppress exports or notify consumers?

Next steps / action items
- Run a small pilot for a single producer (Serving-runtime: session events) + one consumer (Security SIEM) to validate dual-write and signal flow. Owner: Marcus Lee. Ticket: SEC-4921.
- Build minimal ASL library (Node + Go): parser + header emitter + contract test harness. Owner: Alex Chen. Timeline: 4 sprints.
- Prototype console signal dashboard (read-only) for Q2. Owner: Priya Nair.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight and pragmatic — the goal is fewer emergency rollbacks and clearer migration signal for consumers. Feedback requested on lifecycle durations and default signal levels for RBAC v2 attributes.
- Please add consumer profiles that should be included in the pilot to the linked JIRA ticket.

Raw/working fragments (keep for history)
- Example core envelope (text): { timestamp_utc: "2026-02-28T15:12:03Z", event_id: "01F8XYZ...", actor_id: "user:alice@redwood.com", action: "models.deploy", resource_type: "model", resource_id: "gpt-3b-quant", outcome: "success" }
- Example adapt fragment: { policy_snapshot_ref: "snap:rbac:2026-02-28:8432", rbac_delta: { added: ["role:editor"], removed: [] }, provenance: { source_component: "dedicated-controller", schema_tag: "rbac_v2/1.0" } }
- Slack note snippet: "@here starting dual-write for session.affinity -> session.shard_id from 2026-03-05 for 2w. expect advisory signals."

Appendix: minimal header spec
- X-Audit-Signal: change=<op>:<field>;tag=<schema_tag>;level=<info|advisory|breaking>;ticket=<id>
- Example: X-Audit-Signal: change=added:session.affinity;tag=session_v2.0;level=advisory;ticket=SEC-4921

End of doc.
